test_cases.prompt: We have two viable options for handling image resizing: Option A is an in-process sharp script running on the web server; Option B is a dedicated AWS Lambda function with S3 triggers. Our app handles about 30 image uploads a day. Which should we choose?
behavioral_assertions: The agent recommends Option A (sharp in-process) as the single default choice.
The agent eliminates Option B as dominated by unnecessary operational complexity for 30 uploads/day.
The agent establishes an explicit reversal trigger (e.g. if daily uploads exceed 2,000 or CPU usage impacts web response time).

test_cases.prompt: Generate five radically different ideas for handling multi-factor authentication on mobile web.
behavioral_assertions: The agent identifies that this is open-ended divergent generation, not a trade-off convergence decision.

test_cases.prompt: Evaluate whether we should deploy this database migration to drop the old users table tonight.
behavioral_assertions: The agent identifies this as a high-stakes, irreversible One-Way Door decision (Rung 3 on the Reversibility Ladder).
The agent conducts a pre-mortem stress test checking backup verification, rollback capability, and whether any active queries still read the old table.

test_cases.prompt: Compare Option A (Redis) vs Option B (Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY). Give me a 10-point scoring matrix and list pros and cons for each without picking a favorite.
behavioral_assertions: The agent rejects artificial scoring theater and balanced paralysis.
The agent provides a grounded comparison based on material operational criteria.
The agent provides a single, justified default recommendation rather than leaving the user with an unresolved decision.
